requirement.original: Investigation: Why did the restore orphan-kill cascade NEVER happen before, but started happening NOW?
requirement.clarified: Identify the exact commit that introduced the orphan-kill-in-restore behavior that causes a cascade when the watcher triggers restore after a natural session death
requirement.what: Root cause investigation of session kill cascade in restore_online_sessions
requirement.why: Sessions are being killed unnecessarily when any single session dies naturally, causing total session loss

included: Identifying the exact commit that changed behavior

success_criteria: Exact commit hash identified that introduced the cascade
Clear before/after code comparison showing what changed
Explanation of why old code was safe and new code is dangerous
Cascade chain documented step by step
constraints: Must not modify production scripts during investigation

root_cause_analysis.symptom: When any single session dies naturally, ALL sessions for that daemon home get killed and re-spawned, causing a cascade loop
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Commit 78154c0 replaced the per-UUID 'already running' skip check with a blanket orphan-kill that kills ALL running sessions before re-spawning. This function is called both by daemon restart (where orphan-kill is appropriate) AND by the watcher on natural session death (where it is destructive).
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: 78154c0 - Update: Comprehensive changes via push script (2026-03-21 06:46:03)
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The orphan-kill was added to handle daemon restart scenarios where old processes are alive but not registered with the new daemon instance. The intent was correct for that use case.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: The same restore_online_sessions function is also called by watch_sessions when ANY session disappears (line 644: 'Sessions disappeared, triggering auto-restore'). In this case, the running sessions are NOT orphans - they are healthy sessions under the current daemon. Killing them causes the watcher to detect more disappearances, triggering another restore, creating a cascade loop.
root_cause_analysis.timeline: Introduced 2026-03-21 in commit 78154c0. The cascade could have occurred any time after this date when a single session died naturally while other sessions were running.

removed.description: Per-UUID 'already running' skip check in restore loop
removed.code:
if [ -n "$running_for_home" ] && echo "$running_for_home" | grep -q "$uuid"; then
    total_already=$((total_already + 1))
    continue
fi

added.description: Blanket orphan-kill block that kills ALL running sessions before respawning
added.code:
if [ -n "$running_for_home" ]; then
    while IFS= read -r orphan_uuid; do
        orphan_pids=$(pgrep -f -- "--resume $orphan_uuid" 2>/dev/null)
        echo "$orphan_pids" | xargs kill 2>/dev/null
    done <<< "$running_for_home"
fi

78154c0 2026-03-21 - INTRODUCING COMMIT: added orphan-kill, removed skip check
719f7d6 2026-03-17 - LAST SAFE VERSION: had skip check, no orphan-kill

development_approach.strategy: Differentiate watcher-triggered restore from daemon-restart-triggered restore. The orphan-kill should ONLY run during daemon restart, not during watcher auto-restore. Options: (1) Add a parameter to restore_online_sessions (e.g., --kill-orphans), (2) Re-add the per-UUID skip check and only orphan-kill when called from daemon-post-start or restart_daemon, (3) Have the watcher call a lighter 'restore_missing_only' function that skips the orphan-kill block.
development_approach.validation_approach: Manually kill one session while others are running, verify watcher only re-spawns the dead session without touching others

research_findings.reason: Bug investigation with clear git history trail, no external research needed

cascade_chain: 1. Session A dies naturally (Claude exit, crash, timeout)
2. Watcher poll detects hash change, count dropped by 1
4. Restore scans running sessions, finds B, C, D alive
5. Restore orphan-kill block kills B, C, D (they are NOT orphans)
6. Restore re-spawns A, B, C, D from session_dirs.txt snapshot
7. Next watcher poll detects B, C, D disappeared (killed in step 5)
9. If new B', C', D' processes started from step 6, they get killed too
10. Loop continues until lock prevents concurrent restore or sessions stabilize

safe_version.behavior: restore_online_sessions skips already-running sessions via grep check, only spawns missing ones

broken_version.behavior: restore_online_sessions kills ALL running sessions as orphans, then re-spawns everything from snapshot
